create.name: Grateful Living
create.bio:
Grateful Living, run by the nonprofit A Network for Grateful Living, teaches gratefulness as a spiritual practice rather than a polite habit of saying thank you. Its work grows out of the teaching of Brother David Steindl-Rast, the Benedictine monk who founded it, whose view is that every moment comes to us as a gift and that waking up to this makes a person more fully alive. Its staff and guest teachers now carry that work on, as Brother David has retired from public life.

Most of what it offers happens online. Short email series and recorded courses work through themes such as hope, imperfection and spiritual aliveness, a yearly online retreat closes each calendar year, and trained volunteers host monthly Grateful Gatherings in homes, workplaces and places of worship. Its website keeps a free library of reflective practices, daily words and questions, a private journal and a virtual candle, and its YouTube channel holds talks and conversations with Brother David going back many years. Its mailing address is in Amherst, Massachusetts.

courses.title: The Anatomy of Gratefulness (on demand)
courses.description: A recorded course on what living gratefully means beyond counting blessings. It sets out the core ideas and gives daily practices, new language and tools for a more meaningful life, for newcomers and longtime practitioners alike.

courses.title: Grateful Hope (on demand)
courses.description: Six recorded sessions on hope as a grateful stance that faces life's difficulties and stays open to what is possible. Guest teachers including spiritual leaders, authors and a musician share their perspectives alongside daily practices.

courses.title: Revolution of the Heart Online Retreat
courses.description: The yearly online retreat at the turn of the year, held over a Friday evening and a Saturday. Gratefulness practices, music and poetry help participants reflect on the closing year and step into the next one with intention.

courses.title: Stop.Look.Go: A Daily Practice
courses.description: A five-day email pathway on Brother David's three-step practice of pausing, widening one's view and choosing a meaningful next step. It shows how the practice can be brought into ordinary tasks, conversations and transitions.

courses.title: Enliven Your Spirit
courses.description: A five-day email pathway treating gratefulness as a spiritual practice, open to people inside or outside a religious tradition. Each day brings readings, reflections and practices for feeling more present and alive.

free_resources.title: Microscope to Telescope: Expand Your Perspective
free_resources.description: A short guided reflection that takes one thought, looks at it closely and then from a wider angle, to notice connections and meaning that were easy to miss.

free_resources.title: Practice Compassion: Understanding in Action
free_resources.description: A written practice that moves from feeling with others towards acting on their behalf, rooting compassion in an honest look at what one has been given.

free_resources.title: Discovering Meaning in Every Moment
free_resources.description: A three-step reflective practice for noticing the meaning already present in daily life, starting from the recognition that one's life is a gift.
